subject: Repackaging & mid-term uplift for Dedicated capacity (NovaAI)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Miriam Lopez <miriam.lopez@novaai.com>
Cc: procurement@novaai.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity repackaging — initial thinking

Hi Miriam,

Thanks for the time last week. Per our conversation, I sketched three pragmatic packaging options to support NovaAI's increased inference needs while keeping unit cost predictable through your FY. High level — you want more headroom for burst, stronger throughput guarantees for real-time scoring, and an option to lock additional reserve capacity mid-term.

Could you confirm whether the priority is (1) lowest $/token at sustained load, or (2) strict latency SLOs for RPC-style calls? That will change the mix we recommend (larger pool + more aggressive batching vs. more reserved nodes with lower concurrency).

Next step: I can produce a formal quote and pricing workback if you confirm the target baseline QPS and acceptable 95th p99 latency range.

Rough ask for your team:
- Baseline sustained QPS: ~____________
- Typical request size (tokens in / tokens out): ~____________
- Budget cadence (annual/quarterly): FY28 annual

I'll wait for those details and bring Marissa in to draft options.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Miriam Lopez <miriam.lopez@novaai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity repackaging — initial thinking

Hi Rafael,

Thanks — sorry for the delay. Budget cycles and procurement reviews took precedence. Answers below:
- Baseline sustained QPS: 350 requests/sec (avg 12 tokens in, 48 tokens out)
- Latency target: 95th < 220ms for our real-time scoring path; p99 ideally < 450ms
- Budget cadence: annual, but we have a mid-year review in October that could trigger a top-up.

Two immediate asks from procurement (cc'd):
1) Can you outline what discount stacking looks like? We currently have a follow-on renewal in July and would like to combine a mid-term uplift with renewal pricing if possible.
2) Can you provide throughput guarantees and an SLA credit schedule tied to missed p95/p99? Procurement will need this for the SOW.

Also looping in procurement@novaai.com — they'll handle contract redlines and tax details.

Appreciate it,
Miriam Lopez
Head of Product Integrations | NovaAI
miriam.lopez@novaai.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Miriam Lopez <miriam.lopez@novaai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity repackaging — initial thinking

Miriam — thanks for the clarity. Looping in Marissa (AM) and Karthik (pricing/product) to put numbers against the asks. Below are three tailored options; attachments include a pricing workback and an annotated proposal.

Option A — Flex Pool (lower $/token, higher variance)
- Reserved commit: 48 GPUs (A100-class) monthly commit
- Burst capacity: +12 GPUs on demand (subject to availability)
- Pricing: 18% off list for 12-month commit, no additional SLA credits except standard Uptime SLA
- Expected p95 latency: ~260–320ms at baseline; 95th can be improved with aggressive KV cache tuning

Option B — Predictable Throughput (balanced)
- Reserved commit: 64 GPUs
- Burst capacity: +8 GPUs guaranteed for 60s windows
- Pricing: 22% off list for 12-month commit + 5% mid-term uplift credit if you commit to add >=16 GPUs within the contract year
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 350 QPS sustained with p95 < 220ms (see stability appendix)

Option C — Low-latency SLA (performance-first)
- Reserved commit: 80 GPUs with pre-warmed nodes and affinity placement
- Burst capacity: +16 GPUs guaranteed for up to 5min bursts
- Pricing: 28% off list (12-month) or 34% off list (24-month) + SLA credits tiered (p95/p99)
- Throughput guarantee: 350 QPS sustained, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 420ms; includes quarterly performance reviews

Notes on discount stacking: we can combine renewal-year renewal credits with a mid-term uplift if the uplift is executed as an amendment to the existing commit. We typically do a pricing "workback" that converts expected token usage to committed GPU months and proposes a blended discount. See attached pricing_workback.xlsx for a model (line-item assumptions are editable).

Attachments: proposal_v2.pdf (proposal + SOW), pricing_workback.xlsx (model)
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/94821

Next steps: Marissa will draft a formal amendment vs. new contract options and propose exact language for the SLA credits. Karthik, anything to add on the guarantees/penalty bands?

— Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Miriam Lopez <miriam.lopez@novaai.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procurement@novaai.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Revised amendment & pricing — NovaAI (DEAL-94821)

Hi Miriam — following up with the formal amendment options. I took Rafael's Option B as the baseline since it matches your QPS/lower-latency balance. Summary below plus a DocuSign link for the amendment (option B, 12-month).

Chosen baseline: Option B (Predictable Throughput)
- Starting commit: 64 GPUs (A100 equivalent)
- Mid-term uplift: one-time right to add 16 GPUs within 9 months; uplift billed pro-rata for remainder of the month
- Burst guarantee: +8 GPUs available for 60s windows; we guarantee availability 95% of requests for bursts under normal capacity conditions
- Pricing: 22% off list for baseline commit; uplift GPUs priced at 18% off list when executed within the first 6 months; after 6 months uplift will be priced at 15% off list
- SLA credits: tiered schedule included in SOW (p95 miss = 5% monthly credit, p99 miss = 10% monthly credit; exceptions for force majeure and scheduled maintenance)

DocuSign link (amendment for Option B): https://docusign.com/drive/NA-94821-sign
Attachments: proposal_v2.pdf (annotated), pricing_workback.xlsx, redline_terms.docx

Please note: to preserve the quoted uplift pricing bands we need a signed amendment by 2027-05-05; after that the uplift pricing will be subject to current market pricing and may require an additional approval.

If procurement has redlines, please return the redline doc (attached) and we'll triage through legal. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the SLA language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (512) 555-0199

From: Miriam Lopez <miriam.lopez@novaai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novaai.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Revised amendment & pricing — NovaAI (DEAL-94821)

Marissa / Rafael — thanks for the thorough workback. Procurement reviewed the amendment and confirmed they are comfortable with Option B subject to two small asks:
1) Adjust the p95 SLA miss credit to be tiered 3% / 6% (instead of 5% flat) to better reflect degradation bands.
2) Include a single 30-day early termination clause for the first 90 days only if there is a verified region-wide outage affecting >40% of committed capacity for more than 48 hours.

We've attached a redline (redline_terms.docx). If you can accept these minor changes we'll sign the amendment. Also please confirm the pro-rata billing math for the uplift GPUs — procurement wants an example calculation in the amendment.

Assuming we can get the small edits done quickly, we will route the DocuSign to our CFO for signature next week.

Best,
Miriam Lopez
Head of Product Integrations | NovaAI
miriam.lopez@novaai.com
